text:
alex: Heads-up — NovaLabs just sent a shortlist RFP, biggest ask is a drop-in replacement for their current competitor API. They want parity on prompts + deterministic-ish output for business rules. Can we scope a quick POC? :thinking:

maya: Awesome, congrats. Do we have a recommended path — compat shim vs adapter? They want minimal client changes.

alex: Ideally a small compatibility layer that translates competitor payload -> Redwood API. Keep auth header mapping and `response_format` bits. POC target: 2 weeks to show parity on 10 canonical prompts.

sanjay: On the runtime side, note that competitor uses a streaming-first token format that includes interim `finish_reason` fields. We can stream and map to their shape but need to confirm KV cache behavior for their long-context tests.

jess: Re: pricing — NovaLabs asked about per-token parity and a short-term migration discount. Do we offer a credit or temporary unit pricing to match their forecast for the POC?

alex: Sales, propose 25% off hosted rate for 60 days for POC usage up to 5M tokens, then normal pricing. @jess can you confirm if finance ok?

jess: I'll escalate, but we usually do credits instead of price cuts. Will ping finance.

maya: Security questionnaire arrived. They require SOC2 + SSO support + customer-managed KMS for Private. Also an encryption-at-rest detail and a few network diagrams. Attaching the doc from the thread here (PDF). @security-bot any immediate blockers?

security-bot: auto: Received questionnaire (NovaLabs-Sec-2026.pdf). Flag: KMS/HSM integration for on-prem Private deploy. Need input from eng-infra for exact supported providers.

alex: For the POC they said they can accept Hosted if we provide encryption-in-transit + audit log extracts. Private is a later ask. So POC can be hosted with plan to transition.

tom: Quick tech note — prompt parity can be tricky: competitor adds implicit system instructions and normalizes stop tokens. Recommend we run the 10 prompts with both models and record token-level diffs and a small eval rubric (semantic match + business-rule pass/fail). I can instrument the eval harness.

sanjay: Also watch for `nucleus_sampling` vs `top_p` mapping and deterministic seeds. We'll need to map sampling params in shim. I can draft the mapping table.

alex: Example shim curl snippet for their devs (showing header translation):

```
# competitor client -> our shim endpoint
curl -X POST https://shim.example.com/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: CompetitorKey abc123' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"prompt":"Summarize Q1 results","max_tokens":256}'

# shim translates -> Redwood API
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redwood_key>' 
  -H 'X-Client-Id: novalabs' 
  -d '{"input":"Summarize Q1 results","max_new_tokens":256,"sampling":{}}'
```

maya: Nice. Make sure we log both raw competitor request and normalized payload for debugging during POC (redact secrets).

alex: Risk checklist: tokenization differences, streaming framing, function-calling shape (they use `tools` array), and a legal clause about data retention in their contract that wants 30 day logs only.

jess: Legal wants to review retention clause — will loop in contracts. If they insist on hosted but 30-day retention only, engineering must confirm logs export/auto-delete.

sanjay: I can add an auto-delete policy on the dev project for POC, and provide log export hooks. Not a blocker.

maya: Next steps: 1) Sanjay drafts shim param mapping and streaming adapter (ETA 3 days). 2) Tom builds eval harness and example prompt set (ETA 4 days). 3) Jess to confirm POC credit approach with finance (ETA 2 days). 4) Alex to coordinate kick-off with NovaLabs and send SSO/KMS clarifications.

alex: I'll schedule the kickoff for Friday. Thanks all — please drop short updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
